claims.text: Factory's core is the `cplane` package, the scheduler and runner, with its command-line entry point.
Workshop is the owner's console: `factory_ui/` is the Flask app that serves it and `ui/` holds the client it serves from `ui/dist`.
CI's `test` job runs `uv sync --locked` and `uv run pytest` on Python 3.13 with a PostgreSQL 17 service.
Changes under `ui/` run `npm ci`, `npm test` and `npm run build` in `ui/`.
The runtime dependencies in `pyproject.toml` are jsonschema, psycopg 3, Flask and waitress, and `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` are change class 2.
The runner submits work to the platform run API with a role (slice, cut, ticket or review), a mode and the slice's level.
The runner sends answers as messages to the existing run.
The runner sends merge notices as messages to the existing run.
A paused slice's runs are still collected each pass, but no further request or message is sent for it.

Accepted and dropped slices have every run of the job cancelled; a cancellation the platform does not yet accept sets `cancel_pending`, and each later pass calls the cancel again until the entry is cancelled.
Eval attempts stop at the PR boundary and never write slice records or send notices.
`--actor` (default `owner`) names the actor recorded in each mutation's log entry.
Planner mutations persist only through the state update path, which launches no executor.
Moving a slice to ready requires a brief.
Moving a slice from ready to issued requires `--session`, and `--session` is allowed only for that move.
`--force` requires the target planned and a nonempty `--reason`.
Issued and awaiting-handover slices may only have their title and dependencies edited.
A PR touching a class 4 guard path raises merge attention and merges only after the owner's GitHub approval of the current tip.
Workshop is the owner web console and its HTTP API.
`factory_ui/__init__.py` sets `DIST` to `ui/dist`.
The `ui` service serves the React client from `DIST`, which is `ui/dist`.
The Flask app registers routes under `/api/`.
The inbox socket protocol handles arrivals.
`cplane/sessions.py` runs chat turns and `cplane/workshop.py` is the per-turn Workshop tool boundary.
`cplane/runner.py` makes one locked scheduling pass.
`cplane/cli.py` holds the owner and planner commands, installed as the `cplane` command.
`cplane/state.py` validates slice documents against the version 1 schema, `cplane/stores.py` stores them in Postgres, and its `migrate` applies the SQL files of `cplane/migrations/`.
`schema/` holds the JSON Schemas for slices, plans, reviews and claims, and the validators in `state.py`, `cut.py`, `review.py` and `docs_verify.py` load them and validate against them.
Skills are instructions given to chats, cutters, reviewers and the judge.
`cplane/prompts.py` sets `ROOT` to the `cplane/prompts/` directory.
`cplane/docs_verify.py` checks a repository's documentation claims, relations and part graph.
`node/` holds the `factory-cplane` and `factory-restore-check` host wrappers and the fenced CLI image.
`intake` reads one JSON arrival line per connection on a Unix socket server and has no network listener.
The `sessions` service sets `CPLANE_FENCE_COMMAND` to `socket`.
The runner service runs `cplane --actor runner run --every 60`, which repeats a pass and then waits.
State writes are validated against `schema/slices.schema.json` and stored in Postgres.
Inbox arrivals enter the store through the `intake` socket handler and Workshop's `POST /api/inbox`, which both call `inbox_add`.
Chats add features and slices through their Workshop tools: `add_feature` calls `feature_add` and `add_slice` calls `feature_add_slice` on the store.
A runner pass holds the database lock while it collects owner orders, steps the pipeline, routes chat events, collects and delivers each slice, and `run` then writes the bot export.
The runner opens the PR with `self.github.open`.
The runner reads checks with `self.github.checks`.
The runner raises merge attention when `guards` are present.
The runner merges pull requests with `--squash`.
The runner raises `node-step` attention when `node_steps` is not `None`.
The runner submits run requests with `mode` `read` for the review role and `write` for the others.
The runner classifies the PR's changes, requires approval for guard paths, merges, and raises node-step attention when the PR request has node steps.
An owner install request in a slice's log makes the runner start a detached `cplane.deployer` client, which sends an `install` operation to the deployer socket.
After a merge the runner queues `contract-change` attention for declared contract changes and `docs-graph` attention for a failing graph check.
All four services in `compose.yaml` use the same deployer-built image tagged by the deploy commit.
The `ui` service joins the `homelab_default` network.
`node/bin/factory-cplane` runs `cplane` inside the runner container, or the sessions container when the runner is not running.
The run client submits a run with `/v1/runs`.
The runner polls runs with `GET /v1/runs/<id>`.
`docs-verify` asks the platform decisions API for claim verdicts.
The runner requests installs from the platform deployer by starting `cplane.deployer`, which sends an `install` operation over the deployer socket.
`cplane.launcher` is a one-request UNIX socket client.
Workshop reads the platform's `/v1/manage/routes` and `/v1/manage/providers`.
Every service of the root `compose.yaml` uses the image `homelab-deployer-factory:${HOMELAB_DEPLOY_TAG}`, and the deployer passes only `HOMELAB_DEPLOY_TAG`.
After a merge with declared contract changes, the runner raises `contract-change` attention saying each user repository needs an adapting slice in the same feature.
Run request bodies and message bodies Factory builds carry `"contract": 1`; the cancel call sends an empty object.
The run API client calls `POST /v1/runs`, `GET /v1/runs/<id>`, `GET /v1/runs?request_id=`, `POST /v1/runs/<id>/messages` and `POST /v1/runs/<id>/cancel`.
The run API client reads its URL from `CPLANE_EVAL_TASK_URL` and its bearer key from the file named by `CPLANE_EVAL_TASK_KEY_FILE`.
A saved request body is submitted unchanged when its run id is still unknown.
The docs-verify request includes a `text` field.
The docs-verify request has one `support` question.
The docs-verify request sets `repeats` to 3.
The deployer client sends one JSON line with `op`, `application` and a 40-hex `sha`, and reads one JSON line with `ok`, `result`, and on success `application` and `commit`.
The runner's deployer socket path comes from `CPLANE_DEPLOYER_SOCKET`, set to `/run/homelab-deployer.sock` in `compose.yaml`.
The launcher client sends one JSON line per connection to `/run/homelab-launcher.sock`, or the path in `CPLANE_LAUNCHER_SOCKET`, and reads one JSON line back.
Workshop's Home Lab settings endpoint reads `/v1/manage/routes` or `/v1/manage/providers` from `HOMELAB_API_URL` and passes the JSON through.
GitHub requests send `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28`.
GitHub App installation tokens are requested for the named repositories only.
The App id and installation id are read from `CPLANE_GITHUB_APP_ID` and `CPLANE_GITHUB_INSTALLATION_ID`, and the key path from `CPLANE_GITHUB_APP_KEY` (default `/etc/factory/github-app.pem`).
The orders collector reads `<base>/orders` for an `orders` list and posts each result to `<base>/orders/<id>/ack`.
An order has exactly `id`, `created`, `action`, `slice`, `argument` and `expect`, and its action is one of `start`, `slot`, `pause`, `resume`, `answer`, `approve` and `orchestrator`.
The orders base URL comes from `CPLANE_ORDERS_URL`.
The orders collector refuses an order whose fields are not exactly the expected set.

A PR request must have exactly `branch`, `title`, `body`, `node_steps` and `contract_changes`; `node_steps` is text or null and `contract_changes` is null or a non-empty list of `{name, version, users}` with non-empty users.
A saved job request without `contract_changes` is read as null.
`Runner.launch_work` appends the PR request format, including `contract_changes`, to the goal of a slice run.
The brief skill asks for Facts, Fixed decisions, Steps, Allowed changes, Do not, Validation, Git, Escalation and Handover sections.
The ticket builder reads a brief's `## Fixed decisions` and `## Do not` sections and refuses a brief with neither.
`cplane/state.py` validates the state against `schema/slices.schema.json` and also requires unique slice ids.
The slice state schema fixes `version` to 1.
Paths under `schema/` are change class 2.
`cplane/cut.py` loads `schema/plan.schema.json` and validates the cutter's ticket plan against it.
`cplane/review.py` parses the leading fenced JSON of a review and validates it against `schema/review.schema.json`, and `skills/slice-review.md` requests that format.
`cplane docs-verify` reads `docs/claims.json`.
The parser defines `add`, `edit`, `state`, `attention`, `review`, `show`, `pending`, `install` and `docs-verify` commands.
`.github/change-classes` lines are `<class> <pattern>`, gitignore-style from the root; the highest matching class wins and no match is class 1.
`.github/change-classes` is read by the runner before a merge and by the deployer before an install.
The runner reads `.github/change-classes` from the PR's pinned base commit.
The feature export writes only `features/<ID>.md`, `features/<ID>/<ID>-S<n>.md` and, when generated, `backlog.md`; generation is on when `CPLANE_BACKLOG_GENERATED=1`.
Feature export reads `CPLANE_PLANNING_REMOTE` as its remote.
The runner loop runs the feature export at most once per local hour.
The feature export refuses a change to any path its `allowed` method rejects.

After each pass the bot export writes `slices.json` and `slices.json.outbox.jsonl` to `CPLANE_BOT_EXPORT`, mode 0640 with the folder's group, keeping only `BOT_ACCEPTED_FIELDS` for accepted and dropped slices and only `BOT_EVENTS` notices.
The bot export fails when the new outbox does not start with the outbox already written.
The intake socket at `/run/factory-intake/intake.sock` reads one JSON arrival with `text` and optional `fields` and `files` per connection, and replies with `{"id": N}` or an `error` object.
The intake server refuses an arrival with any key other than `text`, `fields` and `files`.
In `compose.yaml` the `ui`, `sessions` and `runner` services each require an env file named after them (`ui.env`, `sessions.env`, `runner.env`).
`compose.yaml` is a change class 4 guard path.
The Postgres store needs psycopg 3 and the system libpq library.
Postgres tests use `CPLANE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, skip without it locally, fail without it under CI, and each test creates its own schema.
The CI, UI and CLI image workflows trigger only on pull requests.
The `test` job runs `uv sync --locked` and `uv run pytest` with a PostgreSQL 17 service.
The `image-gitleaks` job checks out full history, runs gitleaks over it, builds the image and smoke-tests it with a read-only filesystem.
The UI workflow runs on changes under `ui/`, and the CLI image workflow on changes under `node/cli/`, `node/proxy/`, `node/compose.yaml` or `node/check-fence.py`.

The `ci.yml`, `ui.yml` and `cli-image.yml` workflows each have a concurrency group of the workflow name and the PR number with `cancel-in-progress: true`, so a new push cancels that workflow's older run.
The database URL comes from the file named by `CPLANE_DATABASE_URL_FILE`, or else from `CPLANE_DATABASE_URL`, and setting both is an error.
The store facade always returns a Postgres store outside an active transaction.
Postgres connection and operation errors are reported with fixed messages.
`PostgresStore.save` validates the whole state document with `state.validate` before it writes, and `load` validates what it reads.
The store lock is a transaction-scoped Postgres advisory lock.
`migrate` applies `cplane/migrations/*.sql` in name order and records each applied name in `cplane_migrations`, skipping those already recorded.
`import` reads the state file and its outbox and refuses a database that is not empty.
`export` writes state and notices in the file format to a path, which is required when there are notices; otherwise it can write to stdout.
The run folder is named by a hash of the state path under `CPLANE_RUNS`, and relative briefs resolve against the state path's folder.
After a merge, a PR request with node steps raises `node-step` attention on the slice, in both the direct and the tickets flow.
An install request needs an open node-step attention; the owner's request is recorded as `install requested`, a chat's only as `install proposed`.
Workshop's install action records an install request with actor `owner`.
A repository is installable when it is listed in the comma-separated `CPLANE_INSTALL_REPOS`.
The runner starts `cplane.deployer` as a detached child.
The detached child sends the merged commit to the platform deployer on `CPLANE_DEPLOYER_SOCKET`.
The deployer child writes its result in the run folder `installs/` directory.
A held `.started` lock tracks the child, and a child that ends without a result raises an escalation instead of a new install.
After its database dump the deployer runs `cplane migrate` in a new `ui` container, and its health command is the `ui` health command.
When the deployer replies `waits for the owner`, the client's error text names `sudo homelab-deployer install <application> <sha>`, and the runner records that text on the slice as attention.
A successful install answers the node-step attention with `Installed <sha>. Node steps are done. End with kind handover.`

`PostgresStore.migrate` only applies the forward `.sql` files of `cplane/migrations/` in name order and records each name in `cplane_migrations`; it has no down step, so a rollback reinstall does not reverse a migration.
`installed` refuses installable repositories and records a hand install of a merged full SHA.
`ui`'s healthcheck fetches its root page, `intake`'s connects to its socket, and `sessions` and `runner` check PID 1 and run `SELECT 1`.
No healthcheck reads scheduling state: each only fetches the `ui` page, connects to the intake socket, or checks PID 1 and runs `SELECT 1`.
Compose sets the runner service `CPLANE_REVISION` from `HOMELAB_DEPLOY_TAG`.

The request body and request id are saved in the job file before the POST; a lost response leaves no run id, so the saved body is posted again with the same request id, and a request with a run id is only polled.
For an order without a receipt, the runner first records the result failed ("dispatch interrupted") and only then dispatches the order.
A later order pass reuses the result in an existing receipt.
An interrupted dispatch is recorded as failed.
An interrupted dispatch is never repeated.
The platform's `homelab-dump` dumps every database daily, including `factory`.
`factory-restore-check` restores a dump into a container with no network, compares table row counts with the live database, and by default picks the newest `factory-YYYY-MM-DD.dump`.
The loop runs a pass, prints `cplane: run failed` on a failure, waits `--every` seconds, and stops on SIGTERM or SIGINT.
Without `--every`, `run` makes one runner pass.
After every pass the runner writes `slices.json` and `slices.json.outbox.jsonl` of the bot export to the directory in `CPLANE_BOT_EXPORT`.
The first loop pass after 03:45 local time each day exports `factory-YYYY-MM-DD.json` and its outbox to `CPLANE_EXPORT_DIR` with mode 0600, keeping the seven newest.
The runner checks whether an export is due when the local hour changes.
When the local hour changes, the loop calls hourly(path), which is hourly_export.
The feature export renders features and their briefs and pushes the commit to the remote in CPLANE_PLANNING_REMOTE.
The loop keeps `last_day` and `last_hour` only in local variables that start as `None`, so a restart exports again in the same day or hour.
Each pass collects orders right after pulling state, and an empty `CPLANE_ORDERS_URL` skips collection.
An order is dropped with a notice unless the slice exists with the expected state, pause flag and attention kind and time.
Orders are applied through `state.update_locked` with actor `frontline`.
An `orchestrator` order opens a tmux window, and is refused when `CPLANE_FENCE=1`.
Order requests use a ten-second timeout.
`prime` sends one minimal `Reply with: ok` request to Claude and then to Codex.
`install-primer` installs a launchd job for 06:00, 11:00, 16:00 and 21:00, and `uninstall-primer` removes it.
The wake daemon schedules wakes at 05:59, 10:59, 15:59 and 20:59.
Migrations run in file-name order and each applied name is recorded once in `cplane_migrations`.
`migrate` applies only forward `.sql` files in name order and records each name in `cplane_migrations`; nothing in it reverses a migration.
Paths under `cplane/migrations/` are change class 2.
CI's `test` job runs a `postgres:17` service and sets `CPLANE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` to it.
After its dump the deployer runs `cplane migrate` in a new `ui` container.
The claims schema requires `version`, `repository`, `parts`, `claims`, `relations` and `contracts`.
The link test checks the document map's files, relative links and anchors, and the paths cited in `docs/claims.json`.
`--graph-only` checks the schema, citations and graph without calling the decisions API.
After a merge the runner runs the graph check on the merged commit when it has `docs/claims.json`, and queues `docs-graph` attention when it fails.
A run request body names `mode`, `role` and `level` and has no executor field.
Factory owns pull requests.
Factory owns CI.
`factory_ui/__init__.py` imports `Flask`.
`cplane/skills.py` defines `instructions(name)`.
The `frontend` route falls back to `index.html`.

relations.text: The runner loads cplane_slices through state.load.
The runner writes to cplane_slices through the store's save method.
Workshop's API reads and writes Postgres through a `PostgresStore` built from the database URL.
Intake stores each arrival with the store's `inbox_add`.
The sessions service opens a `PostgresStore` for chat turns and their Workshop tools.
Commands write slices through `state.update`, the locked and validated update path.
The store validates state with `schema/slices.schema.json`.
Cut and review requests carry the `cut` or `slice-review` skill from `skills/`.
Sessions install the enabled skills into each new chat workspace with `skills.install`.
After a merge the runner reads the merged commit's claims file and calls the graph-only claims check on it, raising `docs-graph` attention on failure.
`cplane docs-verify` parses the claims check's arguments and runs `docs_verify.command`.
`factory-cplane` runs `cplane` in a running Factory container.
The runner submits, polls, messages and cancels runs on the platform run API.
`docs-verify` posts each claim and relation to the platform decisions API.
The installer connects to CPLANE_DEPLOYER_SOCKET to send one JSON line with op set to install.
The sessions service runs cplane.launcher through its socket fence; cplane.launcher connects to /run/homelab-launcher.sock unless CPLANE_LAUNCHER_SOCKET overrides it.
Workshop requests /v1/manage/routes or /v1/manage/providers on HOMELAB_API_URL.
The runner writes slices.json under CPLANE_BOT_EXPORT after each pass.
The store connects to the platform Postgres with the URL it reads from the service's database URL secret.
The runner parses and validates the final message body as a PR request.
The runner sends a planner's brief as the goal of the slice run and the cut copies its `Fixed decisions` and `Do not` sections into tickets.
docs-verify submits each decision request to /v1/decisions.
